title: Featuring every man in a fourteen-piece band
summary: No single star; all numbers featured band members, unlike small bands.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Okay. How many numbers did you have that would feature just one man in your big band?
You mean as a solo? All the numbers featured some artists, one of the fellas in the band.
There may be several or it may be just one. Yeah, sure.
So for instance, there never was one individual that stood out and the whole number built around him. It was a band. And it featured everyone in the band that could play.

But you go to, you used to go to Louis Armstrong concerts, say in the 50s and the 60s. And he would then, he'd have one number, like he'd have a program built in such a way that he'd feature Buster Bailey on Memphis Blue. But that was a later thing. You never had a star deal.

Yeah, but here's the difference here. There was only five or six pieces there. Mine, I had 14. So you couldn't combine it to one individual. But five piece bands, yes, that's how they had to operate. Well, for instance, the concert last night, it would have been lost if you couldn't feature each individual.
But by being able to feature each individual, it spreads your program over a period of time, which you're looking forward to. And also giving this guy the credit that's doing.
